A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RALU research despite different titles and extensive reformatting. All 28 pages of v2 and 29 pages of v3, including appendices A–E, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures for comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original RALU experiments on FLUX and SD3, including quantitative comparisons, caching integration, ablations, and generated images in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, controlled artifact analyses, design ablations, hardware measurements, and integrations with temporal acceleration and distilled models.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains low-resolution denoising, selective early upsampling using decoded Canny edges, and full-resolution refinement, with correlated noise and JSD-based timestep matching. NT-DM becomes NT-Matching, but its underlying algorithm remains equivalent. Additional positional-embedding explanations and experiments with other acceleration methods do not establish a changed RALU algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 changes T2I-CompBench coverage from complex/texture to spatial/non-spatial/complex and narrows GenEval from six categories to four. CC12M remains. v3 newly identifies MS-COCO for image-quality evaluation, but v2 leaves that data source unspecified, so this alone does not establish an added dataset.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds evaluated FLUX comparisons with Delta-DiT, TeaCache, and TaylorSeer, and SD3 comparisons with Delta-DiT, ToCa, and TaylorSeer. v2 principally compared against ToCa or RAS and Bottleneck Sampling. The integration comparison also replaces the earlier custom caching configuration with named temporal acceleration methods.

E3.justification: FID is replaced by ImageReward, and new artifact-rate and edge-energy evaluations are introduced. The FLUX 4× configuration with 18 RALU steps is replaced by a 5× configuration with 15 steps. New protocols include 100-image artifact analyses, four-step distilled-model integrations, and A6000 benchmarking. The retained FLUX 7× and SD3 stage counts merely change from per-stage to cumulative notation.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends v2's qualitative upsampling-timing study and limited parameter ablations with systematic timing/JSD analyses, artifact rate versus FLOPs, and quantitative ratio sweeps. Appendix C adds image-space versus latent-space edge detection, fixed versus adaptive selection, interpolation comparisons, and edge-mask visualizations. These directly test previously unsupported design choices.

E5.justification: v3 adds error bars in Figures 2–3, a p < 0.001 statement for the ImageReward/JSD relationship, and FLOP mean±standard deviation in Table S4. GenEval reporting changes from fixed-seed wording to four different seeds per prompt. The error-bar definition and significance-test procedure remain unspecified; the wording does not establish increased repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds or replaces extensive results, including ImageReward scores, expanded comparisons, distilled-model integrations, hardware measurements, and artifact ablations. For retained FLUX 7× RALU, reported latency changes from 3.37 to 3.75 seconds, while NIQE 6.87 and CLIP-IQA 0.681 remain unchanged. T2I-CompBench/GenEval change from 0.566/0.646 to 0.633/0.682 under revised task coverage, so these are not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v3 Eqs. (5)–(6) correct the main-text matching target to a latent with isotropic covariance, replacing v2 Eq. (5)'s upsampled-latent target. Appendix A.1 adds consequences for intermediate and fully denoised endpoints. The rescheduling formulas otherwise remain equivalent, and the appendix's inconsistent covariance expressions in Eqs. (S2) and (S4) persist.

C1.justification: The claims of training-free spatial acceleration up to 7× on FLUX and 3× on SD3 remain. However, v3 adds compatibility with timestep-distilled models and elevates combined acceleration up to 15.9× to an abstract claim and principal contribution. Table 2 identifies these speedups as FLOP-based, extending applicability beyond the earlier caching-integration claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds rationales for image-space Canny detection, fixed selection ratios, and nearest-neighbor interpolation. Section 6 introduces a tentative token-merging analogy while acknowledging that mixed-resolution self-attention remains unexplained. Appendix D emphasizes untested U-Net backbones instead of v2's explicit audio/3D examples, while retaining the limitation to flow-matching models.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands execution and reproduction information: FP16, torch.profiler, FlashAttention except for ToCa, A6000 memory measurement, 5,000 MS-COCO images, explicit selection ratios, and configurations for new baselines and distilled-model integrations. These disclosures do not prove earlier settings differed. The front-page access pointer changes from a code repository to a project page, and the old custom-caching instructions disappear.

R1.justification: v3 adds context on Latent-SR and image-space super-resolution, forecasting methods, and token merging, alongside references supporting new metrics and implementations. FID and VQ4DiT references are removed. These additions refine the positioning, while the central distinction from training-dependent approaches and Bottleneck Sampling remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, artifact discussion, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. NT-DM is renamed NT-Matching, experiments gain dedicated artifact and edge-selection sections, and a Discussion section is introduced. Appendices are reorganized and references move after them, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 switches to a two-column layout, redraws the framework diagram, merges the main benchmark tables, restructures integration displays, and adds quantitative artifact plots and appendix tables. Qualitative comparison panels and captions are revised. Some SD3 and FLUX 7× appendix images are retained and relocated, rather than newly added results.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence for the central artifact-mitigation claims through controlled analyses and design-choice ablations, addressing v2's reliance on mostly qualitative artifact examples. Broader competitive baselines, integration tests, and execution details also improve assessment and reproducibility. FID removal and changed task subsets limit direct score comparisons, and reporting inconsistencies remain, such as FLUX 7× NIQE being 6.87 in Table 1 but 6.51 in Table 3. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
